items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: I had a very good piano player -- a guy named Sonny. Oh he was excellent. And we played at [Alabama?] and other places that was requests.

ctx.x: Oh, no they don't help you get no jobs. Now lately you could go and stand in downstairs if you want to stay there the whole day and see who they call for -- need a drummer -- we need a bass player. Then wheresever up they get the first come, first served. But now they got a new system that they, when someone calls in, senior citizen or somethin' calls in for a group, you're on line, they have a rotation thing goin'. So, I made one last week so I guess I was up that near it'll be a long time before they get round…

I first learned how to play I was called a ... request -- I played a request house. That means you play for tips more than your salary. And people throw throw songs at you your grandmother don't even know and you're got to try to remember. I had a little trick, I used to say well -- I had a very good piano player -- a guy named Sonny. Oh he was excellent. And we played at [Alabama?] and other places that was requests. They would send up money -- we would make twenty, twenty-five dollars a piece -- five piece…
What would you say are some of the highlights of your career?
